name: Piece of Krom'zar's Banner
summary: A torn strip of cloth taken from the standards of Warlord Krom'zar, commander of the Kolkar retaliatory force. It serves as tangible proof to Regthar Deathgate that the centaur invasion from Desolace has been broken.

sections.title: Trophy of the Centaur Incursion
sections.body: Following the systematic defeat of Kolkar chieftains across the Barrens, a furious warband marched east from Desolace intent on revenge. Led by Warlord Krom'zar, these invaders assaulted the defensive bunkers west of the Crossroads. Slicing a remnant from the warlord's fallen battle standard provides undeniable proof to Regthar Deathgate that the assault was crushed and the southern trade routes preserved for the Horde.

faq.q: What is this banner piece used for?
aliases: what do i do with banner piece
faq.answer: The torn cloth is brought to Regthar Deathgate at his bunker west of the Crossroads. It proves that Warlord Krom'zar was slain and his raiding force shattered, concluding the defense of the northern Barrens.
Krom'zar was a fierce Kolkar commander sent from the wastes of Desolace. He led a direct counter-assault against Horde outposts in response to the deaths of the local Kolkar leaders.

faq.q: Why did the Kolkar attack the bunker?
faq.answer: After Horde champions eliminated the local Barrens chieftains—including Barak, Verog, and Hezrul—the enraged centaur rallied reinforcements from Desolace to exact vengeance on the Horde presence west of the Crossroads.

faq.q: Does Thrall hear of this victory?
faq.answer: Yes. Upon receiving the banner fragment, Regthar Deathgate promises to send formal word directly to Warchief Thrall in Orgrimmar, commending the defenders who broke the invasion.

angles.text: Defeating Krom'zar and claiming his colors halts a major centaur offensive, securing the northern corridors between Durotar, Mulgore, and the Crossroads.
Centaur aggression has long plagued the nomadic tribes, making the destruction of Krom'zar's vanguard a welcome sign of security for the trails leading toward Mulgore.
